subject: chemistry_2
question_text: What is the cross linking agent used in vulcanisation?

verification.note: Unit 12 (Polymers), printed as VSAQ 10 on book p.97. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board scheme, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Source: the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", printed chapter 9 (POLYMERS), book pp.95-98 (PDF pp.34-37), which is unit 12 in this bank. The chapter is VSAQ-only: it prints 24 Very Short Answer Questions and has no Short Answer and no Long Answer section at all, and no PROBLEMS. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK WORDING: the printed answer is "5% sulphur is the cross linking agent" with the scheme "Raw rubber + S → vulcanized rubber". Written that way the percentage reads as part of the name of the agent. The agent is sulphur; 5% is the proportion used for the flexible rubber of tyres and about 30% gives ebonite, and both figures are stated here. GAP: the book never says what the sulphur cross links join to, namely the leftover double bonds of the cis-1,4-polyisoprene chains, and never names the monomer of natural rubber, which is isoprene, 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene; both are supplied.

steps.why: Sulphur is used because it can insert between two chains at their leftover double bonds, forming a cross link that belongs to both. The percentage is not part of the name of the agent; it sets how many cross links form and therefore how hard the product is.
common_mistakes: Writing 5% sulphur as though the percentage were part of the name. The agent is sulphur; 5% is the amount used for tyre rubber.
Naming a different agent such as oxygen or chlorine. The syllabus answer is sulphur.
steps.memory_tip: One word answers the question: sulphur. The percentage only sets how hard the rubber becomes.
steps.margin_note: The single word sulphur earns this mark. Add the temperature range if there is room.

steps.why: Raw rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene, and each repeat unit still has one C=C bond left after polymerisation. Those are the points where sulphur forms the cross links, which is why only diene rubbers can be vulcanised.
common_mistakes: Writing that sulphur joins the monomers together. The chains are already formed; sulphur joins one chain to another.
Writing that vulcanised rubber melts more easily. The cross links raise the softening temperature.
steps.memory_tip: The cross links run between chains, not inside a chain.
steps.margin_note: The equation together with the words cross links finishes this mark.

insider_note: The question asks for one substance, so the first word must be sulphur. Everything after that is protection for the second mark.
